- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent prices are rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in sentiment; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion is evident in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is 2–3% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.5%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag behind true trend by 1–3 days; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch momentum.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; match forecast slope to sentiment polarity shift.
